summary: The milestone completed 4 experiments in 0.8 minutes, including 3 compute-bound experiments. The official-live llama.cpp model report-channel forensic capture set the critical path at 0.78 minutes, while the locked task-level indicator recorded no compute-bound GPU-idle event.
bottlenecks_identified: The official-live llama.cpp model report-channel forensic capture consumed nearly all reconstructed milestone wall time.
Disk-mtime reconstruction exposes end-to-end durations but no phase-level evidence explaining why the report-channel capture was longest.
No task-window correlation connects the point-in-time GPU snapshot to a named compute-bound experiment, preventing a defensible utilization-efficiency finding.
No model-concurrency or runner-selection evidence is available, so DualGPURunner applicability cannot be audited.
improvements_suggested: Emit task-scoped phase timings for model startup, inference, report capture, and teardown.
Sample GPU utilization, memory, and process identity inside each compute-bound task window and attach the samples to that experiment's artifact.
Record model count and selected runner at launch, validating DualGPURunner only when multiple models are loaded concurrently.
Add post-task accelerator-process lifecycle reporting so allocated but inactive processes can be distinguished from active experiment work.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add experiment-correlated phase and GPU telemetry to the research conductor's operational artifacts.
Instrument the report-channel forensic workflow to isolate startup, inference, capture, and teardown cost.
Persist launch-time model concurrency and runner selection, plus post-task process cleanup status.
meta_reflection: The reconstructed timing identifies the critical path but does not explain its phase cost. The point-in-time GPU report cannot establish compute-task efficiency or a missed parallel-runner dispatch without experiment-window and model-concurrency correlation, so no nonzero savings estimate is supported.
